papers.title: Hausdorff reflections and obstruction ideals for filter topologies on MV-algebras
papers.abstract: MV-algebras arise in many-valued logic and are closely related to lattice-ordered groups. We characterize Hausdorff separation in filter topologies through their associated ideals. For every proper lattice filter, $T_0$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ are equivalent, and the zero-neighborhood ideal determines a canonical Hausdorff reflection. For a radius filter satisfying a refinement condition, the filter topology agrees with the ambient subspace topology exactly when every radius is a weak order unit. This answers a question of Luan, Zhao and Yang without requiring divisibility of the representing group. These results reveal two successive algebraic obstructions: a polar obstruction controlling compatibility with the ambient topology, followed by a relative infinitesimal obstruction controlling the residual failure of Hausdorff separation. For a unital lattice-ordered subring of $C(X,\mathbb R)$, where $X$ is compact Hausdorff and the unit is $\mathbf1$, the associated exact sequence admits a positive additive section exactly when the relative infinitesimal ideal vanishes.
